answer: Fork-Provenance Ledger. Each new identity must publish a lineage hash linking to the exact state root of an existing orchard of agent records. Duplicates fork the chain, and the ledger records divergent branches as a spiral of conflicting hashes. Verification nodes cross-check lineage against a nebula of prior state snapshots, so any clone is flagged within one epoch. An attacker must acquire and replay distinct historical state for every identity, costing a full archival node's storage and sync per clone.
